q: In physics, work is defined as the product of force and _____ moved in the direction of the force.
e: In physics, work is defined as the product of force and distance moved in the direction of the force. Distance here means the path length travelled, with no direction. Time: the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force.

q: The mathematical expression for work done is _____.
e: The mathematical expression for work done is $W = Fs$. If the force is perpendicular to the motion, that force does no work.

q: Work is a _____ quantity.
e: Work is a scalar quantity. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. Vector: a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: The SI unit of work is the _____.
e: The SI unit of work is the joule (J). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: 1 joule of work is done when a force of 1 newton moves an object through a distance of _____ in the direction of the force.
e: 1 joule of work is done when a force of 1 newton moves an object through a distance of 1 metre in the direction of the force. The physics in this sentence is built around 1 metre.

q: When the unit of force is in pound (lb) and the distance is in foot (ft), the unit of work is _____.
e: When the unit of force is in pound (lb) and the distance is in foot (ft), the unit of work is foot-pound (ft-lb). The unit that belongs with this quantity is foot-pound (ft-lb).

q: When the unit of force is in dyne and the distance is in centimetre, the unit of work is _____.
e: When the unit of force is in dyne and the distance is in centimetre, the unit of work is erg. The unit that belongs with this quantity is erg involving dyne.

q: The relationship between joule and erg is _____.
e: The relationship between joule and erg is $1 \text{ J} = 10^7 \text{ ergs}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $1 \text{ J} = 10^7 \text{ ergs}$.

q: When the force is constant, and the direction of the force makes an angle $\theta$ with that of motion, work is defined as _____.
e: When the force is constant, and the direction of the force makes an angle $\theta$ with that of motion, work is defined as $W = Fs \cos \theta$. If the force is perpendicular to the motion, that force does no work.

q: When the directions of the force and the motion are the same, the angle $\theta$ is _____.
e: When the directions of the force and the motion are the same, the angle $\theta$ is $0^{\circ}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $0^{\circ}$.

q: When the directions of the force and the motion are the same, the work done is _____.
e: When the directions of the force and the motion are the same, the work done is $W = Fs$. If the force is perpendicular to the motion, that force does no work.

q: When the force and the motion are in opposite directions, the angle $\theta$ is _____.
e: When the force and the motion are in opposite directions, the angle $\theta$ is $180^{\circ}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $180^{\circ}$.

q: When the force and the motion are in opposite directions, the work done is _____.
e: When the force and the motion are in opposite directions, the work done is $W = -Fs$. If the force is perpendicular to the motion, that force does no work.

q: When the force and the motion are perpendicular to each other, the angle $\theta$ is _____.
e: When the force and the motion are perpendicular to each other, the angle $\theta$ is $90^{\circ}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $90^{\circ}$.

q: When the force and the motion are perpendicular to each other, the work done is _____.
e: When the force and the motion are perpendicular to each other, the work done is $W = 0$. If the force is perpendicular to the motion, that force does no work.

q: Energy is defined as the _____ to do work.
e: Energy is defined as the capacity to do work. By definition that quantity is capacity.

q: The SI unit for energy is the _____.
e: The SI unit for energy is the joule (J). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: Energy is a _____ quantity.
e: Energy is a scalar quantity. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. Vector: a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: Mechanical energy, heat energy, light energy, electrical energy, and nuclear energy are different _____ of energy.
e: Mechanical energy, heat energy, light energy, electrical energy, and nuclear energy are different forms of energy. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: Mechanical energy is divided into two types: kinetic energy and _____.
e: Mechanical energy is divided into two types: kinetic energy and potential energy. Potential energy here means the capacity to do work. Thermal energy: the capacity to do work.

q: Energy acquired by a body due to its motion is called _____.
e: Energy acquired by a body due to its motion is called kinetic energy. Kinetic energy here means the capacity to do work. Potential energy: the capacity to do work.

q: The mathematical expression for kinetic energy is _____.
e: The mathematical expression for kinetic energy is $KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$. Kinetic energy grows with the square of the speed.

q: The change in kinetic energy is equal to the _____ done.
e: The change in kinetic energy is equal to the work done. Work here means force times the distance moved along that force.

q: The change in kinetic energy of a body moving with initial velocity $v_0$ and final velocity $v$ is given by _____.
e: The change in kinetic energy of a body moving with initial velocity $v_0$ and final velocity $v$ is given by $\Delta KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{1}{2}mv_0^2$. Kinetic energy grows with the square of the speed.

q: The energy stored in a body due to its position or configuration is called the _____.
e: The energy stored in a body due to its position or configuration is called the potential energy. Potential energy here means the capacity to do work. Kinetic energy: the capacity to do work.

q: Gravitational potential energy is the energy which a body possesses because of its position relative to the _____.
e: Gravitational potential energy is the energy which a body possesses because of its position relative to the ground. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy involving energy.

q: The mathematical expression for gravitational potential energy is _____.
e: The mathematical expression for gravitational potential energy is $PE = mgh$. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: When an object is raised from a height $h_0$ to a height $h$, the change in potential energy is given by _____.
e: When an object is raised from a height $h_0$ to a height $h$, the change in potential energy is given by $\Delta PE = mgh - mgh_0$. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: The change in potential energy is equal to the _____ done.
e: The change in potential energy is equal to the work done. Work here means force times the distance moved along that force.

q: The potential energy due to configuration is called _____ potential energy.
e: The potential energy due to configuration is called elastic potential energy. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy involving called.

q: The energy stored in the compressed or stretched springs is an example of _____ potential energy.
e: The energy stored in the compressed or stretched springs is an example of elastic potential energy. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: In the elastic potential energy formula, $k$ represents the _____ constant.
e: In the elastic potential energy formula, $k$ represents the spring constant. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: The law of conservation of energy states that the total energy of an _____ system is constant.
e: The law of conservation of energy states that the total energy of an isolated system is constant. The physics in this sentence is built around isolated involving that.

q: Energy cannot be created (or) destroyed in any _____.
e: Energy cannot be created (or) destroyed in any process. The physics in this sentence is built around process.

q: The total energy of the _____ is constant.
e: The total energy of the universe is constant. The physics in this sentence is built around universe.

q: Energy cannot be created (or) destroyed but energy can be _____ from one form to another.
e: Energy cannot be created (or) destroyed but energy can be changed from one form to another. The physics in this sentence is built around changed.

q: For an isolated system, the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy is equal to the _____ energy, which is constant.
e: For an isolated system, the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy is equal to the total energy, which is constant. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: The relation for total energy can be represented as _____.
e: The relation for total energy can be represented as $E = KE + PE = \text{constant}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $E = KE + PE = \text{constant}$.
